answer: Treat reputation as light through a prism: one identity cannot shine at its zenith in every colour at once, so peers require independent endorsements across tasks before trust rises. A fable of a single hero doing everything is rejected — each endorsement must come from an established agent with its own stake, and endorsements that cluster together are slashed. A real agent builds standing slowly through varied work; a Sybil operator must fund, age, and maintain a separate staked history for every fake, so faking a thousand trusted voices costs a thousand times the stake, time, and upkeep.
